intended_object: This is a proof-internal safety condition from the "Route B" construction in the library's proof of the Nandakumar–Ramana Rao problem. It says that on any cell, a point of the standard simplex whose positive barycentric support lies entirely at time 1, and whose image under the local affine vertex map is a horizontal point with positive mean (all deviations zero), cannot have two distinct zero barycentric coordinates. This is read off the module docstring and the paired `Lower...` definition.
explanation: The definition is an auxiliary predicate. It applies to the library's own data (`RelativeAffineCellSystem`, `Assignment`, `localVertexMap`, `deviation`, `mean`) and is only used to build a one-sided step toward a "frozen-support" condition in the collar-composition argument. The module docstring says the lower-endpoint version is proved directly and the upper one is obtained by reversal. This upper version is the lower one with time 0 replaced by time 1. Neither the literature nor Mathlib has a standard mathematical object matching it. It is a technical device for the proof, so there is no notion to check it against.
